To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
i.c.v. ouabain alone elicits a rise in BP and HR and a cardiac arrhythmia of ventricular origin, and that i.c.v.-propranolol attenuates/prevents this response.
(+/-)-propanolol, (+)- propanolol and UM-272 (but not lignocaine), antagonize the cardiovascular effects of i.c.v. ouabain.

the central beta-adrenoceptor antagonist propranolol, in addition to its well-known peripheral beta-adrenergic blocking activity, has a direct neural depressent effect which can be demonstrated by its ability to attenuate/prevent the cardiovascular effects of the central neuroactive drug ouabain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of propranol and ouabain in the central nervous systems (CNS) with special reference to the neurally mediated effects on the cardiovascular (C.V.S.) system.
the interaction of ouabain with (+)- and (+/-)-propanolol in the CNS.
the interaction of ouabain with propranolol, a beta-blocking agent and local anesthetic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural depressant effect is due to an interference with the depolarization process of the nerve membrane and/or a neuronal blocking action.
the antagonism of propranolon to the cardiovascular effect of ouabain is not a result of local anesthetic activity or beta-adrenergic blocking activity.
the neural depressant effect of propranalol is not due to local anesthetic action, but rather due to a direct depressant action on neural tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

propranolol and its enantiomers and UM-272 exert a direct neural depressive effect on the central nervous system which is independent of their local anesthetic and beta-blocking activities and which can antagonize the cardiovascular effects of centrally-administered ouabain.
ouabain and (+/-)-propanolol interacted in the brainstem to elicit a depressant effect on the central nervous system which resulted in a blockade of ouabain-induced cardiac arrhythmias.
propranolol, by virtue of its depressant effect on the nervous system, can prevent the cardiovascular effects of cardiac glycosides in the CNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural depressant effect is an important mechanism of action of beta-blockers in the central nervous sytem.
propranolol and its analogues have a neural depressant action that is not due to beta-adrenoceptor blocking or local anaesthetic activity.
propranolol, in addition to its well-known beta-blockade activity, may have a direct neural depressor activity that may be useful in the management of arrhythmia.
